feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so it states no outcome for it. Evidence: iteration 0 (five 12 mm sensors, x ±0.024 m, y 0.04 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, mass 0.6 kg, kp 4.0) scored 96.84 with max_error 0.063 to 0.070 m and line loss 1 (oval, slalom) and 2 (s-bend). Iteration 1 (seven sensors, x ±0.036 m) scored 91.28, with max_error still 0.062 to 0.068 m and line loss about 1. Iteration 2 (wheel_track 0.14 m, mass 0.5 kg, kp 7.0) scored 74.95, with slalom line loss rising to 1.9. Iteration 3 (16 mm footprints, y = 0.03 m, plus the iteration 2 drivetrain) scored 48.12, the lowest so far, with line loss 1.25 on the s-bend. Because iteration 3 changed the sensor size, the forward row and the drivetrain together, its result cannot be attributed to any single change. Per the contract, turn rate is the wheel speed difference divided by wheel_track, so a narrower track gives more yaw per unit of turn command. The wider 0.14 m track therefore reduced turn authority, consistent with the lower scores of iterations 2 and 3. Next race (this geometry is iteration 0's): if the score is at or above about 96.8 and max_error is still above 0.06 m on the s-bend, the limit is turn authority, so narrow wheel_track to 0.10 m with mass 0.6 kg. If line_loss_events stay at 2 on the s-bend, change sensor_size to 0.016 m at the same five x positions and y 0.04 m, so the change is sensing-only. If the score falls below about 96, the controller rather than the geometry is the cause, so report the controller settings you used.
requested_changes: If the score is near 96.8 and max_error stays above 0.06 m on the s-bend: narrow wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.10 m, keeping mass 0.6 kg and the five-sensor layout. Cite iteration 2, where widening to 0.14 m dropped the score from 96.84 to 74.95, and the contract relation that a narrower track gives more yaw per command.

If line_loss_events stay at 2 on the s-bend with the five sensors: set sensor_size to 0.016 m, keeping x = -0.024 to +0.024 m and y = 0.04 m and changing nothing else. This isolates the footprint effect, which was confounded with the look-ahead and drivetrain changes in iteration 3.

If the score drops below about 96 on this baseline: do not change the geometry. Report the controller settings and telemetry so the Integrator can separate controller from geometry effects, rather than moving wheel_track or mass again.
